[A10] **Owner decisions, 2026-10-06.** These replace the corresponding lines of the issue body.

1. **Start now.** #664 no longer waits for the end of the protocol-processor program. It is a documentation-only lane and runs in parallel with the processor work and the #665 firmware lanes.
2. **AECP moves to the core with the rest (option a).** ADP, ACMP, MAAP, SRP and AECP, including unsolicited notifications and counters, run on the bare-metal core in the Mark II default. The fabric keeps framing and timestamps, the gPTP plane, the media path and the ingress filter. The "unless the owner rules otherwise" line for AECP is resolved this way.
3. **Default flip.** The documents describe the split as the Mark II default and the all-fabric build as a supported option. The build switch flips to the split only after F2 to F5 (#665) pass the bench: all streams, all counters and the audio soak. Until then the all-fabric build stays the shipping default, and the documents say so explicitly, so the tree holds no contradiction.
4. **VERSION major 3 lands with the default flip, not in this PR.** 0x0003 identifies only images that run the split. #664 states the version-3 rule and the five-simulation landing plan, and leaves VERSION at major 2.

Acceptance items 1, 2 and 4 stand. Item 3 moves to the default-flip PR. The owner approves the requirement text before merge.

[A10] **Lane for #664: Mark II requirements, documents only.** Executor [A548], branch `664-mark2-reqs` from dev `423ac5d9`. Reviewers [R508] (internal) and [R509] (external). The owner decisions in 6009576644 replace the matching lines of the issue body.

**Items:**
1. **Ownership and placement** (`REQUIREMENTS.md` section 1).
   - ADP, ACMP, AECP (including unsolicited notifications and counters), MAAP and SRP become build-selectable placements.
   - The Mark II default is the bare-metal core. The all-fabric build is a supported option, and it is the shipping default until the switch flips after F2 to F5 pass the bench. Say so explicitly.
   - The fabric keeps framing and timestamps, the gPTP plane, the media path and the ingress filter.
2. **FR_NFR** (`docs/reference/FR_NFR.md`).
   - Rewrite NFR-SCOUT-01 (the single control hart and how stream capacity grows) and NFR-SCOUT-02 (who owns protocol control).
   - Rewrite NFR-SCOUT-03. For each moved path, a bounded firmware service latency inside its normative timeout replaces "never on firmware service latency". Derive each bound from the clause that sets the timeout, and cite the clause number. Use `docs/spec-refs.md` and the in-repo extracts first.
   - Define each path's test hook: where the latency is measured, from mailbox RX to TX commit.
   - Audio and gPTP deadlines stay fabric-only.
   - Update every row these trace to.
3. **The split document** (`docs/ARCHITECTURE_HW_SW_SPLIT.md`).
   - Give the ownership rule for each placement.
   - Describe the mailbox interface: several packet mailboxes; block RAM rings, a doorbell and one interrupt; 32-bit accesses, no DMA; a bus adapter per host; portable C behind a small HAL; one YAML contract. Cite `docs/design/MAILBOX_SPLIT.md` and `docs/reference/MAILBOX_CONTRACT.md` (F0), and the saved-state boot read and apply (F1).
   - State the bare-metal-first rule and the unit-test rule (#665 5992455815, 6008744385).
4. **No contradiction in the tree.**
   - Grep every document that cites these rows or states the old ownership: "never on firmware", "fabric-only" for these protocols, the AECP placement. Correct each one.
   - Regenerate the traceability matrix with its generator. Never hand-edit generated files.
5. **Version.** State the version-3 rule (`0x0003` identifies only images that run the split) and the five-simulation landing plan for the default-flip PR, including the `>> 16` major check in `tb/verilator/hostplane`. VERSION stays at major 2 in this PR.
6. **Owner approval.** PR-BODY.md gets a section titled "Requirement text for owner approval". It shows every changed requirement row as old text and new text, side by side.

**STOP conditions:**
- Any change outside documentation, requirement tables, traceability generators' outputs and docs gates' registrations. STOP and name it.
- A normative timeout you cannot cite. STOP with the list.

**Gates:**
- the full docs-check set on the committed head: `docs/traceability/gen_module_matrix.py --check`, `check_wire_accountability`, the requirement/traceability checks, TOC and style;
- the 48-command builder set, because docs-only PRs get the bank too.

All gates rc 0. Output: HANDOFF.md and PR-BODY.md ("Relates to #664" until the owner approves; the manager switches it to Closes at approval). Then post REVIEW READY with the head on #664. Do not push.

Do not edit or delete any existing comment.

[A548] TAKEN

Executor: [A548]. Independent reviewers: [R508] internal and [R509] external.
Authoritative references: #664 assignment 6009584763 and owner decision 6009576644; #665 directives 5992455815 and 6008744385; #640; merged F0 #668 and F1 #669; REQUIREMENTS.md, FR_NFR.md, the split and mailbox contracts, and docs/spec-refs.md.
Interpreted scope: documentation-only Mark II placement and timing requirements for ADP, ACMP, AECP including notifications and counters, MAAP and SRP; bounded service hooks and regenerated traceability. All-fabric remains the shipping default until F2 to F5 pass the bench. VERSION remains major 2; major 3 is documented for the default flip.
Validation plan: full docs-check set and the 48-command builder bank on the committed head, with independent gates run concurrently and recorded separately. No push. Requirement wording awaits owner approval.
Blockers: none established; stop if any necessary change exceeds the authorized document scope or a normative timeout cannot be cited.

[A548] STOP
Head: `423ac5d910d09ab189b3acc39ae3ae1d10d50b19` on `664-mark2-reqs`. No repository edits or commits; worktree clean. No push.

Invoking assignment 6009584763: "A normative timeout you cannot cite. STOP with the list."

I cannot cite a numeric normative response timeout for these moved paths:
- AECP successful-command and asynchronous unsolicited notifications: Milan v1.2 5.4.5.2 and IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.5.2 prescribe notification behavior and immediate ordering, without a numeric maximum delivery interval. The solicited-command 240 ms bound in 9.3.2.6 is not a separate unsolicited delivery deadline.
- GET_COUNTERS unsolicited delivery: Milan Table 5.22 limits notifications to one per descriptor per second. This is minimum spacing, not maximum event-to-notification latency.
- MAAP received PROBE to DEFEND: IEEE 1722-2016 B.3.3, B.3.5.5 and B.3.6.6 define the transition and transmitted fields without a numeric response timeout. B.3.4.2 and Table B.8 define the interval between probes, not a new response window from local receipt.
- ADP SHUTDOWN to ENTITY_DEPARTING: Milan v1.2 5.6.3.5.8 and 5.6.3.5.11 prescribe the send without a numeric shutdown-to-transmit timeout.

Decision needed before drafting: supply the numeric clauses, or authorize explicitly labeled project service budgets for paths whose standards specify immediate action, ordering or cadence without a numeric maximum response latency. Those budgets must preserve the standards obligations and must not be presented as normative timeout values.

The assigned docs/spec-refs.md is absent at this base. Available in-repository clause transcriptions were consulted first, then the standards PDFs for the missing wording. F0's existing mailbox-access bounds are conditional and are not measured target-time bounds.

HANDOFF.md and PR-BODY.md are written in the assigned output directory. They record the unchanged requirement rows, available timing constraints and derivations, proposed RX/event-to-TX-commit test hooks, all 606 contradiction-search hit records with dispositions, and the gate table. Repository gates and the 48-command builder bank are NOT RUN: STOP preceded any candidate edit. No green validation or contradiction-free-tree claim is made. Requirement wording and both independent reviews remain outstanding.

[A548] REVIEW READY
Commit: a27808375427859dc357f6bfd0a88842062b20ed
Branch: 664-mark2-reqs, from 423ac5d910d09ab189b3acc39ae3ae1d10d50b19; not pushed.

Changed: 21 documentation files. All five control functions are build-selectable, including AECP notifications and counters. All-fabric remains supported and the shipping default until F2 to F5 acceptance. The requirement register proposes one T_svc = 10 ms project budget with per-path clause derivations, seven test hooks, and independent normative ordering/spacing/deadline obligations. The split architecture covers F0, F1, bare-metal-first, FT and the later VERSION-3 landing plan. VERSION is unchanged.

Validation: the full 48-command bank plus all remaining docs-workflow, imported-documentation and no-git checks ran on this committed head: 91 command receipts, all rc 0. Traceability regenerated byte-identically; the no-drift, wire-accountability, requirement/traceability, TOC and style checks passed. The full builder ran with --require-rv32 and returned rc 0.

Validation limits: the vendor-analysis entry explicitly SKIPPED in the disposable container with no analyzer. Builder gate 11 calibration was NOT RUN because the historical mf48 placement-utilization report is absent; its other arms passed. No Vivado, simulation build or bench operation was performed. These are not claimed as measured passes.

Acceptance evidence: HANDOFF.md records every changed requirement old -> new, each timing derivation and hook, all 617 base / 643 candidate contradiction-search hits with dispositions, the gate table and artifact digests. PR-BODY.md follows the template, uses Relates to #664, and includes the exact Requirement text for owner approval. Both are in the assigned output directory, below 200 KB. The worktree is clean.

Open approval: the owner must approve the requirement text and the proposed 10 ms budget. Independent reviews [R508] and [R509] remain pending. The assignment's retired major-check suite is absent at the base; the documented default-flip plan carries its VERSION >> 16 assertion into a live suite alongside all five current VERSION simulations. No executable, firmware, test, VERSION or build-script changes.
